evidence.excerpt: Spot and preemptible instances offer substantial per-hour cost reductions for cloud compute but introduce job interruption risk that can increase total cost when checkpointing is not implemented. We built a cost model for WGS alignment and variant-calling pipelines that incorporates hourly spot price distributions sampled over 90 days from two cloud providers, mean time to interruption distributions per instance family, and checkpoint overhead for BWA-MEM2 and GATK stages. Simulations over 500 synthetic cohort scenarios (50–1000 samples, 10×–30× coverage) showed that naive use of spot instances without checkpointing increased effective cost by 18–34 % relative to on-demand pricing in high-volatility markets. A bidding and checkpoint strategy derived from the model reduced pipeline cost by 41 % on average relative to on-demand in stable price periods. We validated the model against actual billing records from a 200-sample pilot run. The model is implemented as a Python library with a command-line interface.
